test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 22 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Anjani can do a certain piece of work in 30 days. Anjani and Khushbu can together do the same work in 10 days, and Anjani, Khushbu and Sushmita can do the same work together in 9 days. In how many days can Anjani and Sushmita do the same work together?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(30, 10, 9) = 90 units.

Efficiency of Anjani = 90 ÷ 30 = 3 units/day.

Efficiency of (Anjani + Khushbu + Sushmita) = 90 ÷ 9 = 10 units/day.

Efficiency of (Anjani + Khushbu) = 90 ÷ 10 = 9 units/day.

Efficiency of Sushmita = 10 − 9 = 1 unit/day.

Time for Anjani + Sushmita = 90 ÷ (3 + 1) = 90 ÷ 4 = 45/2 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 45/2 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Anjani (A) = 30 days

Time taken by Anjani and Khushbu (A + K) = 10 days

Time taken by Anjani, Khushbu and Sushmita (A + K + S) = 9 days

Total Work is taken as the LCM of all given days: LCM(30, 10, 9) = 90 units.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**

 Anjani (A)
 30
 90

 A + K + S
 9
 90 ÷ 9 = 10
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of S = Efficiency of (A + K + S) − Efficiency of (A + K)

⇒ Efficiency of S = 10 − 9 = 1 unit/day

⇒ Combined efficiency of A and S = Efficiency of A + Efficiency of S

⇒ Combined efficiency of A and S = 3 + 1 = 4 units/day

⇒ Time taken by A and S = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 90 ÷ 4 = 45/2 days

**∴ The correct answer is 45/2 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns

Works on the same logic as Time & Work. Inlet pipes have positive efficiency, and outlet (emptying) pipes have negative efficiency.

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in direct proportion to the actual amount of work done. If people work for the same number of days, wages are proportional to their efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

When individuals work on alternate days, calculate the work done in one complete cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 people) and divide total work by cycle work to find the number of cycles.

MDH Formula

For groups of people doing work: (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂.
